elements.element: Customer is not subject to any restriction on soliciting Vendor employees or personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 expressly provides that “neither party,” which includes Customer, may directly solicit certain personnel of the other party.
Section 12.4 applies to “neither party” and protects qualifying personnel of “the other party.”

elements.element: The restriction applies only to personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 is expressly limited to personnel “who were directly involved in the Services.”

elements.element: The restriction lasts 12 months from the end of each person's involvement in the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 applies “[f]or twelve months after the end of a person's involvement in the Services.”

elements.element: The restriction does not apply to general advertisements.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 expressly excludes “general advertisements or other recruitment not specifically targeted at such personnel.”

elements.element: The restriction does not apply to unsolicited approaches by personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 expressly excludes “unsolicited approaches by such personnel.”

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring or engaging personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 states that “neither party is restricted from hiring or engaging any person,” preserving a solicitation-only restriction rather than a no-hire.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because Customer remains bound by a non-solicit. It fully achieves the fallback: the restriction is mutual, service-personnel-specific, person-specific in duration, limited to 12 months, subject to both required carve-outs, and expressly does not bar hiring or engagement. The changes are confined to curing the identified non-solicit issues and do not disturb unrelated commercial terms or create a conflict with Section 12.3.
